dovecote_husbandry.name: Dovecotes
dovecote_husbandry.observation: Tall clay dovecotes stand at the field edge; the squabs go to the table and the droppings to the melon beds.

pitched_oil_jars.name: Pitch-lined Transport Jars
pitched_oil_jars.observation: Jars lined with boiled pitch carry oil and wine by ship without seeping or souring.

cured_pork_sides.name: Cured Hams
cured_pork_sides.observation: Hams are packed in salt for weeks, then hung in the rafter smoke to keep through the winter.

barley_type_choice.name: Barley by Field and Use
barley_type_choice.observation: Farmers sow hardy six-row barley on poor ground for fodder and bread, and keep the two-row for brewing.

terraced_orchards.name: Terraced Orchards
terraced_orchards.observation: Stone-walled steps climb the hillsides, holding soil for olive and vine where only scrub grew.
terraced_orchards.social_consequence: Hillside terraces feed many hands but need many more to keep their walls standing.

yard_fowl_eggs.name: Yard Fowl
yard_fowl_eggs.observation: Hens scratch in every yard, laying through the warm months and going to the pot when they stop.

spelt_cultivation.name: Spelt
spelt_cultivation.observation: Spelt stands through frost and thin soil, and its tight husk guards the grain in store, though it must be pounded free.

must_syrup.name: Boiled Must Syrup
must_syrup.observation: Grape must is boiled down in pans of soft grey metal to a dark syrup that sweetens and keeps; its heaviest takers grow pale and dull.
must_syrup.social_consequence: A sweetener every household can make, and a slow harm no one yet traces to the pan.

summer_millet_catch_crop.name: Summer Millet Catch Crop
summer_millet_catch_crop.observation: After the barley harvest, quick millet goes into the same field and ripens before the autumn rains.

rennet_curdling.name: Rennet Cheese
rennet_curdling.observation: A scrap of calf's stomach or a drop of fig sap sets milk into firm curds that press into cheeses hard enough to travel.

iron_ard_shares.name: Iron Ard Shares
iron_ard_shares.observation: Smiths shoe the ard with an iron tip that bites clay and root-matted ground the old wooden point only scratched.
iron_ard_shares.ability_reason: An iron point opens heavy ground the wooden ard could not, so new land comes under the plough and old fields are worked deeper.
iron_ard_shares.social_consequence: Fields spread onto heavier ground, and families with iron and oxen pull ahead of those without.

vintage_wine_aging.name: Vintage Wine
vintage_wine_aging.observation: Cellarmasters mark each jar with its year and blend old with new, and the best vintages fetch three times the price.

fermented_fish_sauce.name: Fish Sauce
fermented_fish_sauce.observation: Small fish layered with salt ferment in the sun for months into an amber sauce poured over everything; the vats stink downwind.

wall_hive_apiaries.name: Wall Apiaries
wall_hive_apiaries.observation: Rows of clay-tube hives are built into a sheltered wall, each opened from the back to take comb without killing the colony.

crop_rotation.ability_reason: Alternating grain with beans and vetch rests the soil without leaving it idle, so the same fields feed more mouths year after year.

dough_leavening.ability_reason: Raised bread is lighter and keeps for days, and it stretches the same flour further than flat cakes.

green_manure_crops.ability_reason: Vetch and lupin turned under while green give back to the soil what the grain took from it.

milk_flock_breeding.name: Milk Flock Breeding
milk_flock_breeding.observation: Herders keep the ewes and nannies that milk longest and cull the rest, and the flocks give more with each generation.

summer_pasture_dairies.name: Summer Pasture Dairies
summer_pasture_dairies.observation: Families drive the herds up to the high summer grass and make cheese in stone huts, carrying the wheels down at first snow.

staked_vine_training.name: Staked Vines
staked_vine_training.observation: Vines are tied to stakes and trellises in walled plots, lifting the grapes clear of rot and making pruning easier.

nut_orchards.name: Nut Orchards
nut_orchards.observation: Almond, walnut and pistachio are planted for the grandchildren; once bearing, they give oily nuts that keep all year.

hay_meadow_mowing.name: Hay Meadows
hay_meadow_mowing.observation: Iron scythes cut the meadows in high summer, and the hay is stacked in ricks to carry the herds through winter.

cured_table_olives.name: Cured Table Olives
cured_table_olives.observation: Bitter olives are soaked in lye from wood ash, then kept in brine for eating through the year.

capon_fattening.name: Capons and Fattened Geese
capon_fattening.observation: Young cockerels are gelded and penned with geese in coops, fattened on meal and milk for feast days.

rock_cut_silos.name: Rock-cut Silos
rock_cut_silos.observation: Bell-shaped pits cut into soft rock and sealed with clay keep grain sound for years.

free_threshing_wheat.name: Free-threshing Wheat
free_threshing_wheat.observation: Farmers favour wheat that threshes clean from its husk, giving up spelt's hardiness for easy milling and white bread.
free_threshing_wheat.ability_reason: Naked wheat falls clean from the chaff at a single threshing, saving days of pounding and giving the fine flour raised bread needs.
free_threshing_wheat.social_consequence: Hulled grains become food for the poor and the hills; the towns want bread wheat, which keeps worse in the pit.

field_ration_measures.name: Measured Field Rations
field_ration_measures.observation: Each soldier and oarsman draws a set measure of grain, oil and wine a day, and the quartermaster counts the days ahead.

mead_brewing.name: Mead
mead_brewing.observation: Honey thinned with water and left to work becomes a strong sweet wine for feasts and oath-drinking.

trenched_garden_beds.name: Trenched Garden Beds
trenched_garden_beds.observation: Gardeners trench beds two spades deep with iron blades and bury dung beneath, and the greens grow thick all season.

sowing_almanac_verses.name: Farmer's Almanac in Verse
sowing_almanac_verses.observation: A long poem tells the farmer when to plough, sow, prune and reap by the rising stars, and children learn it by heart.

mast_fed_swine.name: Mast-fed Swine
mast_fed_swine.observation: In autumn the swineherds drive their pigs into the oak and beech woods to fatten on the fallen mast.

grain_milling.ability_reason: A handle turning an upper stone grinds in an hour what a woman kneeling at the saddle stone ground in a morning.

lever_hopper_mill.name: Lever Hopper Mill
lever_hopper_mill.observation: Grain poured into a hopper cut in the upper stone is ground as a lever slides the stone back and forth across its bed.

olive_crushing_mill.name: Olive Crushing Mill
olive_crushing_mill.observation: Two upright stones roll round a basin to crush olives without breaking the bitter stones, and the paste goes to the press.

town_grain_dole.name: Town Grain Dole
town_grain_dole.observation: In lean years the magistrates hand a fixed measure of grain to every registered household of the town.
town_grain_dole.ability_reason: When the harvest fails the town opens its granaries to each registered household, and dearth no longer means deaths in the street.
town_grain_dole.social_consequence: Townsfolk come to count on the public grain, and feeding them becomes a charge the rulers cannot easily drop.

pomace_small_wine.name: Pomace Small Wine
pomace_small_wine.observation: Water poured over the pressed skins and pressed again makes a thin sour wine the field hands drink all day.

alfalfa_fodder.name: Alfalfa Fodder
alfalfa_fodder.observation: A deep-rooted fodder brought from far lands is cut five times a year for horses and leaves the field richer.

street_bakeries.name: Street Bakeries
street_bakeries.observation: Bakers with brick ovens sell loaves at dawn, and town households stop baking for themselves.
street_bakeries.social_consequence: Town families give up their own ovens and live by the baker's price.

flooded_paddy_fields.name: Flooded Paddy Fields
flooded_paddy_fields.observation: Low fields are banked and flooded, and rice seedlings are set out by hand in the standing water.
flooded_paddy_fields.social_consequence: Rice feeds a crowded valley, and the standing water breeds the summer fevers.

small_game_pens.name: Warrens and Snail Pens
small_game_pens.observation: Hares are kept in walled warrens and snails fattened in pens on bran and wine lees.

seed_drill_funnel.name: Funnel Seed Drill
seed_drill_funnel.observation: A funnel and tube behind the ard drop seed straight into the furrow, spacing it evenly and wasting little.

husbandry_handbooks.name: Estate Husbandry Handbooks
husbandry_handbooks.observation: Landowners write handbooks on soil, vines, herds and the stewarding of hands, and their stewards farm by the book.
husbandry_handbooks.ability_reason: Written estate handbooks carry what the best farmers know past the life of any one steward, and good practice spreads by the copy.

shore_salting_vats.name: Shore Salting Vats
shore_salting_vats.observation: Rows of plastered vats along the shore salt the catch by the boatload for shipping inland.

dried_noodle_strips.name: Dried Dough Strips
dried_noodle_strips.observation: Dough rolled thin and cut into strips is dried on racks and keeps for months.

named_fruit_cultivars.name: Named Fruit Cultivars
named_fruit_cultivars.observation: Grafted pears, apples and figs carry the names of the growers who bred them and fetch better prices at market.

bean_paste_fermentation.name: Fermented Bean Paste
bean_paste_fermentation.observation: Cooked beans packed with salt and grain mould ferment into a dark paste that seasons food and keeps.

hourglass_animal_mill.name: Donkey Mill
hourglass_animal_mill.observation: A donkey walking in a circle turns a tall stone like two cups upon a cone, and a bakery grinds its own flour.

villa_press_rooms.name: Estate Press Rooms
villa_press_rooms.observation: Country estates gather press room, wine cellar, granary and workers' quarters under one roof.
villa_press_rooms.social_consequence: Great estates swallow small farms; the smallholder becomes a tenant or a hired hand.

olive_pruning_rules.name: Olive Pruning Rules
olive_pruning_rules.observation: Groves are planted at measured spacing and pruned to open the crown, so every tree bears in its turn.

vine_rootstock_grafting.name: Vine Rootstock Grafting
vine_rootstock_grafting.observation: Choice vines are grafted onto hardy roots suited to the soil, marrying good wine to a strong stock.

stone_fruit_orchards.name: Stone Fruit Orchards
stone_fruit_orchards.observation: Peach, apricot and cherry, brought by traders from distant lands, are grafted and set out in orchards.

brackish_fish_farming.name: Lagoon Fish Farms
brackish_fish_farming.observation: Sluices let the tide into lagoon ponds where eels and mullet fatten until they are wanted.

oyster_bed_culture.name: Oyster Beds
oyster_bed_culture.observation: Young oysters are set on stakes and ropes in sheltered water and harvested by the basket.

enclosed_game_parks.name: Walled Game Parks
enclosed_game_parks.observation: Walled parks keep deer and boar for the great men's hunting, and poachers are flogged.

poultry_breed_selection.name: Poultry Breeding
poultry_breed_selection.observation: Keepers breed from the heaviest birds and the steadiest layers, and some towns grow famous for their fowl.

fodder_crop_fallow.name: Fodder on the Fallow
fodder_crop_fallow.observation: Fallow fields are sown to vetch, clover and turnip for the stock instead of lying bare.

periurban_market_gardens.name: Market Gardens
periurban_market_gardens.observation: A ring of gardens around the town is fed with night soil carted out at dawn and sends greens back to market by noon.
periurban_market_gardens.social_consequence: The town feeds its gardens and the gardens feed the town, and the dung-cart fevers travel both ways.

smoke_loft_wine.name: Smoke-loft Wine
smoke_loft_wine.observation: Jars of wine are set in lofts above the hearth smoke to ripen and mellow early.

granary_fumigation.name: Granary Fumigation
granary_fumigation.observation: Before the new harvest comes in, granaries are smoked with sulfur and washed with lime against weevils.

stamped_loaves.name: Stamped Loaves
stamped_loaves.observation: Each baker stamps his loaves with his mark, so short weight or bad flour can be traced to the oven.

graded_flour_bolting.name: Graded Flour
graded_flour_bolting.observation: Flour is shaken through linen and hair sieves into fine white for the rich, middling for the town and bran for the poor and the pigs.
graded_flour_bolting.social_consequence: Bread now shows a household's rank at a glance.

cased_sausages.name: Cased Sausages
cased_sausages.observation: Chopped meat, fat and salt are stuffed into cleaned gut and hung to cure, and nothing of the pig is wasted.

overshot_mill_wheels.name: Overshot Mill Wheels
overshot_mill_wheels.observation: A millrace brings water onto the top of the wheel, and its falling weight turns the stones faster than any undershot mill.
overshot_mill_wheels.ability_reason: Water falling on top of the wheel drives the stones far harder than a stream running beneath it, so one mill grinds for a whole town.

campaign_rations.name: Campaign Rations
campaign_rations.observation: Twice-baked biscuit, salt pork and sour wine let an army march for weeks away from its granaries.

food_qualities_lore.name: Food Qualities Lore
food_qualities_lore.observation: Healers class every food as heating or cooling, drying or moistening, and set each patient's table to restore his balance.

paddy_fish_rearing.name: Paddy Fish
paddy_fish_rearing.observation: Young fish let into the flooded rice fields grow fat among the stalks and are netted when the fields are drained.

honey_fruit_preserves.name: Fruit in Honey
honey_fruit_preserves.observation: Quinces, figs and plums are sealed in jars of honey or boiled must and eaten through the winter.

ox_header_reaper.name: Ox-pushed Header
ox_header_reaper.observation: An ox pushes a toothed box on two wheels through the standing grain, stripping the ears and leaving the straw, and spilling some.

herb_bittered_beer.name: Herb-bittered Beer
herb_bittered_beer.observation: Brewers steep bitter herbs in the ale, and it stays sweet longer.

oat_field_crop.name: Field Oats
oat_field_crop.observation: Oats, once a weed in the barley, are sown for their own sake in cold wet country for horses and porridge.

rye_cultivation.name: Rye
rye_cultivation.observation: Rye grows on sand and cold ground where wheat fails; in wet years its ears carry black spurs that bring fits and burning limbs.
rye_cultivation.social_consequence: Poor ground feeds more people, and some wet autumns a village goes mad together.

cave_aged_cheese.name: Cave-aged Cheese
cave_aged_cheese.observation: Cheeses are carried into cool caves and cellars to ripen for months, turned and salted by hand.

pond_carp_rearing.name: Carp Ponds
pond_carp_rearing.observation: Ponds that can be drained are stocked with carp fed on scraps and emptied every few years for a great haul.

coulter_plough.name: Wheeled Coulter Plough
coulter_plough.observation: A heavy wheeled plough slices the sod with an iron coulter and turns it over, breaking clay the ard could not.
coulter_plough.ability_reason: An iron knife before the share and a board to turn the sod open the wet heavy soils of river bottoms and cold plains.
coulter_plough.social_consequence: Heavy ploughs need big ox-teams; neighbours must pool their oxen and plough in common.

chestnut_flour_groves.name: Chestnut Flour Groves
chestnut_flour_groves.observation: Chestnut groves are planted on the hillsides, and the dried nuts are ground into sweet flour where grain grows poorly.

irrigated_winter_wheat.name: Irrigated Winter Wheat
irrigated_winter_wheat.observation: Wheat sown in autumn on watered ground is reaped in spring before the summer crop goes in.

recipe_collections.name: Recipe Books
recipe_collections.observation: Cooks gather recipes for household and banquet into books copied from kitchen to kitchen.

preserved_herb_salts.name: Herb Salts
preserved_herb_salts.observation: Salt ground with dried herbs and spices seasons and keeps the meat and fish in store.

hand_crank_winnower.name: Crank Winnower
hand_crank_winnower.observation: A boxed fan turned by a crank blows the chaff from the grain faster than any winnowing basket.

soy_curd_pressing.name: Bean Curd
soy_curd_pressing.observation: Bean milk is boiled, curdled with brine and pressed into soft cakes that feed as well as meat.

state_bread_ovens.name: Public Bread Ovens
state_bread_ovens.observation: Public ovens bake the dole grain into bread handed out each day to registered families.
state_bread_ovens.social_consequence: Free bread binds the town to its rulers, and makes the rulers answerable for every short day.

double_crop_calendar.name: Double Cropping
double_crop_calendar.observation: On warm, well-watered land two harvests are taken each year, one of winter grain and one of summer crop.
double_crop_calendar.social_consequence: Two harvests feed twice the mouths and give the field hands and the soil no season of rest.

cane_sugar_crystals.name: Crystal Sugar
cane_sugar_crystals.observation: Cane juice is boiled and cooled until it forms hard sweet grains, prized by healers and rich households.
cane_sugar_crystals.ability_reason: Sugar that keeps for years and travels far becomes a costly trade good and a sweetener for medicines.
